title: Launch your adventure
description: Bring a player, a setting, and a choice into one small game.

tasks.title: Connect the pieces into a game
tasks.body: You now know how to display a scene, store a value, ask for input, and choose a path. Combine them in order: set the scene, ask for a name, ask for a direction, then reveal an ending.
tasks.detail: Keep each input response in its own variable. Use the player’s name in a printed message. Then use if/else to give left and right different endings. Test both paths before sharing your game.

tasks.code:
print("A floating island appears.")
hero = input("Your name? ")
print("Welcome aboard, " + hero)
path = input("Left or right? ")
if path == "left":
    print("You befriend a cloud dragon.")
else:
    print("You discover a sky garden.")
tasks.output:
A floating island appears.
Welcome aboard, Nova
You befriend a cloud dragon.
tasks.note: The same code welcomes different players and produces two endings. That is your first interactive adventure.

tasks.question: What should you test before sharing the adventure?
tasks.why: Different replies exercise different behavior. Testing names and both paths catches mistakes a single run might miss.

tasks.prompt: Remix the floating island into your own world. Change both endings and try different player replies.
Build your own adventure. Print an opening scene, ask for a name and welcome that player, then ask for left or right and use if/else for different endings. Your story words are up to you.
tasks.starter:
# Print your opening scene
hero = input("Your name? ")
# Welcome your hero by name
path = input("Left or right? ")
# Use if/else for two different endings
hints: Four parts, in order: an opening scene, a welcome that uses the name, the path question, and two different endings.
Each comment in the starter marks where a print() or the if/else goes. Fill them in from top to bottom.
Patterns from earlier lessons: print("Welcome, " + name) for the welcome, and if answer == "yes": then else: for the two endings.

error_hints.text: The player's name is stored in hero, and the path in path. Use those exact names.
Lines inside if and else start with four spaces.
Your very first line must be a print() with a scene, before the line that asks for a name.
Keep both input() lines from the starter: the name first, then the path.

similar_example.code:
print("The train doors open.")
rider = input("Ticket name? ")
print("All aboard, " + rider)
similar_example.note: A scene, a question and a welcome. Your adventure adds the path question and two different endings.

other_ways.code:
print("A storm rolls in.")
hero = input("Your name? ")
print(f"Welcome aboard, {hero}!")
path = input("Left or right? ")
if path == "left":
    print("You ride the lightning.")
else:
    print("You shelter in a lighthouse.")

messages.message: Add an if condition and an else block, with an indented story message in each.
Ask for the player name first and the path second, using two input() calls.
Welcome the player using their input name, then reveal the ending.
Left and right currently tell the same story. Give the if and else blocks different discoveries, and compare the input variable with "left" or "right".
Start by printing an opening scene before asking the player for their name.

Your adventure opens with a scene, welcomes players by the name they type, and gives left and right different endings. You combined all four Python skills! Read both endings: do they finish the story you started?
